criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given a patient encounter, when the AI generates a note, then the clinician can review and approve it.
Given a clinician rejects a note, when they provide feedback, then the system logs the action in the audit trail.
Trust: The audit trail must show the AI's note and the clinician's approval or rejection.

stories.notes: Added approve_encounter_note and reject_encounter_note MCP tools. Audit trail (audit_log.jsonl) is the single source of truth for note status (generate_note -> approve_note|reject_note keyed by note_id), so approval/rejection is always traceable back to the AI draft it decided on.

criteria.text: Given an AI recommendation, when a clinician approves it, then the action is logged in the audit trail.
Given a clinician edits a recommendation, when they save changes, then the edit is logged in the audit trail.
Trust: The audit trail must reflect all AI recommendations and clinician actions.

stories.notes: Added edit_encounter_note, logging a distinct edit_note audit entry separate from approve/reject. approve_encounter_note and reject_encounter_note now default to the latest saved edit (via a shared _current_note_text helper) rather than always the AI original, so the audit trail accurately reflects what the clinician actually reviewed when they decided. Criterion 1 (approve logged) was already satisfied by STORY-001 approve_encounter_note; this story closes criteria 2 and 3.

criteria.text: Given a low-confidence recommendation, when the AI flags it, then the clinician sees a warning icon.
Given a flagged recommendation, when the clinician reviews it, then they can manually input corrections.
Trust: The system must log flagged recommendations and clinician corrections.

stories.notes: No UI exists in this build, so REQ-008's "visual warning" is implemented as a structured warning field on GeneratedNote (agreed interpretation with user) rather than a rendered icon -- whatever client calls the MCP tool is responsible for surfacing it. generate_encounter_note now requires a confidence score (0.0-1.0, threshold 0.7 per user); below threshold, confidence_reason is mandatory (ToolError if omitted) so the flag always carries an explanation per REQ-008's exact wording. Manual correction reuses edit_encounter_note from STORY-002 rather than rebuilding it, per the brief's explicit instruction.

criteria.text: Given encounter data, when the AI suggests codes, then the clinician can review and approve them.
Given a code suggestion, when the clinician rejects it, then they can provide feedback for improvement.
Trust: The audit trail must log code suggestions and clinician decisions.

stories.notes: Added suggest_codes, approve_codes, reject_codes MCP tools, mirroring STORY-001's note workflow exactly (audit-log-as-source-of-truth via a new _find_suggestion helper, one decision per suggestion set, idempotent replay, ToolError on conflicting redecision). Code suggestions are tied to an existing note_id from generate_encounter_note, reusing its confirmed patient/encounter context rather than re-verifying identity. No external ICD-10/CPT validation database exists in this system -- correctness (the "Incorrect code suggestions" failure path) is mitigated by clinician review/reject-with-feedback, same honest limitation as STORY-001's note generation, not by algorithmic checking.

criteria.text: Given encounter data, when the AI identifies a care gap, then it flags it for clinician review.
Given a flagged care gap, when the clinician addresses it, then the action is logged in the audit trail.
Trust: The system must log identified care gaps and clinician actions.

stories.notes: Added identify_care_gaps and address_care_gap MCP tools. Deliberately NOT bundled like STORY-004's codes -- discussed the tradeoff with the user first (bundling would misrepresent partial progress, since a clinician might resolve one care gap today and leave another flagged for weeks from the same encounter). Each description passed to identify_care_gaps becomes its own CareGap with an independent gap_id and its own audit trail via a new _find_gap helper; address_care_gap records free-text resolution rather than an approve/reject binary, since addressing a care gap is not a yes/no on an AI recommendation. Same idempotent-replay / one-closing-action-per-gap / ToolError-on-conflict guarantees as the rest of the codebase. No external clinical-guideline database exists -- false positives in care gap identification are mitigated by clinician review, not computed.

criteria.text: Given a FHIR API endpoint, when the system requests patient data, then it retrieves and displays the data.
Given an EHR system, when the system integrates with it, then it remains EHR-agnostic.
Trust: The system must log all data retrieval actions from EHRs.

stories.notes: This is the first story with a real external system dependency. Registered a Backend Systems app in Epic on FHIR (fhir.epic.com), generated an RSA key pair for SMART Backend Services JWT-assertion auth (private key kept strictly local and gitignored, only the public JWKS committed), and confirmed the real non-production FHIR base URL and OAuth2 flow end-to-end via a manual smoke test (meshmedic-mcp/verify_epic_sandbox.py, run by hand -- not part of the automated pytest suite, since it makes a real network call and unit tests must stay I/O-free per the repo's testing rules) against Epic's open sandbox with synthetic test-patient data. New epic_fhir_client.py module (separate responsibility from the MCP tool definitions) handles token exchange + Patient.Read. New fetch_patient_from_ehr MCP tool added as a standalone capability rather than reworking search_ehr_patient/get_patient_chart, to avoid regressing STORY-001 through STORY-005 which depend on the existing local sample_patients.py ID space -- Epic's real FHIR IDs are a different, unrelated ID space. oracle_health honestly raises ToolError (not connected) rather than faking a result, satisfying "remains EHR-agnostic" via a shared interface without pretending a second real connection exists. Every call, success or failure, is audited.

criteria.text: Given an AI recommendation, when the clinician requests a source citation, then the system highlights the relevant transcript section.
Given a citation request, when the system cannot provide it, then it explains the reason.
Trust: The system must log all citation requests and responses.

stories.notes: Added request_citation(note_id, claimed_excerpt), verifying a claimed citation against the note's stored transcript rather than trusting the calling model's claim -- directly guards against the "incorrect citation provided" failure path, not just "citation missing". A new _find_citation helper does a whitespace/case-tolerant but non-fuzzy regex match (normalizes claimed_excerpt whitespace, escapes it, swaps escaped spaces for s+, case-insensitive search against the original transcript) so trivial formatting differences do not cause false "not found" results while paraphrasing still correctly fails to match -- deliberately not fuzzy/semantic matching, since a threshold-based approach could pass a citation that only loosely relates. Works uniformly across notes/codes/care-gaps since all three share the same note_id/transcript chain -- no separate tool needed per recommendation type. Returned character offsets are the "highlight" mechanism for a system with no UI (same approach as STORY-003's warning field). Every request is audited regardless of outcome. Documented an honest limitation in the tool's own docstring: this proves an excerpt is not fabricated, not that it is definitively the true basis for the recommendation -- there is no semantic-grounding system in this build.

criteria.text: Given an AI recommendation, when the system displays it, then it shows a confidence score.
Given a low-confidence recommendation, when the clinician reviews it, then they see an explanation for the low confidence.
Trust: The system must log all confidence scores and clinician interactions.

stories.notes: STORY-008 maps to the same REQ-008 text as STORY-003 (flagged to user before building) -- for notes specifically, STORY-003 already satisfied all 3 criteria (GeneratedNote always returns confidence; warning/confidence_reason on low ones; audited). User chose to extend confidence scoring to code suggestions and care gaps too, rather than call it done notes-only, so "AI recommendation" is covered generically, not just notes. suggest_codes gained confidence/confidence_reason (one score per suggestion set, mirrors generate_encounter_note). identify_care_gaps changed its descriptions:list[str] parameter to gaps:list[CareGapInput] (confidence is per-gap, not per-call, consistent with STORY-005's decision that gaps are addressed independently -- one encounter can surface both a high- and low-confidence gap). All gaps in a call are validated before any audit entry for that call is written, so a call is all-or-nothing rather than partially recorded if one gap fails validation. Both new paths reuse the existing CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD constant and warning-string format from STORY-003, no new confidence logic invented. Updated all existing identify_care_gaps test call sites for the new signature; all 33 pre-existing tests still pass (no regression).

criteria.text: Given a patient encounter, when the AI generates a note, then the review time is under 2 minutes.
Given a note review, when it exceeds 2 minutes, then the system provides suggestions to speed up the process.
Trust: The system must log documentation time for each encounter.

stories.notes: documentation_time_seconds (elapsed time from generate_note to the approve_note/reject_note decision, REQ-012) is computed in approve_encounter_note and reject_encounter_note, written into that decision's audit-trail entry, and returned on the response along with exceeded_target and, once the 2-minute target is exceeded, a fixed suggestions list. Idempotent replay reuses the stored duration rather than recomputing against a new 'now'.

Given a note review, when it exceeds 2 minutes, then the system provides suggestions to speed up the process.
Trust: The system must log documentation time for each encounter.

criteria.text: Given a compliance audit, when the system is reviewed, then it meets all relevant standards.
Given a security breach attempt, when the system detects it, then it prevents unauthorized access.
Trust: The system must log all compliance checks and security incidents.

stories.notes: "Meets all relevant standards" names no specific external standard anywhere in this project's docs, so this is scoped (agreed with user) as an internal, code-checkable control checklist rather than a certification claim: run_compliance_check() replays audit_log.jsonl against 4 named controls -- audit completeness (REQ-006), single-decision integrity (REQ-014), security-incident logging completeness (REQ-011), and a static no-PHI-in-structured-logs scan (REQ-011, added after user review to close a flagged scope gap) -- and writes its own compliance_check audit entry. "Unauthorized access" is scoped to this server's one real access boundary (read_transcript_file's roots guard against path traversal); its denial audit entry carries an explicit security_incident:true tag rather than being inferred from error_class alone, so it can't be confused with unrelated AccessDenied business-rule conflicts elsewhere in the file. Third failure path ("system fails to log incidents"): _append_audit_entry now catches OSError, logs it with a stable AuditLogWriteFailure error_class to the structured stderr stream, and re-raises ToolError rather than letting a caller report an action as done when its audit entry was never actually written. Verified end-to-end with a real manual run (not just pytest): generate+approve a note, trigger a genuine roots-guard denial, run run_compliance_check() over the real resulting audit_log.jsonl -- all 4 controls passed against real data.

outstanding: Given a compliance audit, when the system is reviewed, then it meets all relevant standards.
Given a security breach attempt, when the system detects it, then it prevents unauthorized access.
Trust: The system must log all compliance checks and security incidents.

Given a clinician has reviewed a referral letter, when they approve it, then the system marks it as ready to send.
Trust: The system logs the creation and approval of each referral letter for audit purposes.

Trust: The system logs the source of each piece of information presented to the clinician.
